caption: The drawing displays two rectangular wooden boxes, each shown in a separate horizontal section labeled “Front View—Wooden Lock” (top) and “Back View—Showing Works” (bottom). Both illustrations depict the same object from different perspectives. The front view shows a light tan or beige box with four visible screws at the corners and a large black keyhole in the center. The wood grain is faintly visible, and the surface has a smooth, lightly shaded finish. The back view reveals the inner workings of the lock, with a similarly shaped wooden box but with additional mechanical features, including a metal or grayish plate centered around the keyhole, two triangular metal brackets on each side, and a metal rod or lever running diagonally across the upper central portion. The back panel is mainly tan with shaded metal parts; screws secure the brackets, and the central metal lock piece has a rectangular shape. Both sections are drawn with outlined structures and differentiated by the use of brown, gray, and black shading to indicate wood and metal parts. The illustration is signed “J. Gynard 1903” at the bottom right.
title: Lock
